venue.name: Ladysmith Museum
venue.description: The Ladysmith Museum is run by the Ladysmith and District Historical Society, a volunteer non-profit that also runs the Ladysmith Archives and the Industrial Heritage site. It sits at 721 1st Avenue in downtown Ladysmith, in a town-owned building that holds the museum, a gift shop, a gallery and a downstairs Learning Centre. Permanent displays cover the cultural, educational, medical, business and industrial development of the town, with artifacts from the mining and lumber industries and the railway. Admission is free and volunteers are on hand to answer questions.

facility_notes.washrooms: The Learning Centre features a level entrance, bathroom, small kitchenette, and blue screen for photography.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: A wheelchair ramp is available, thanks to the Town of Ladysmith.

venue.hours_notes: Open Mon-Fri 10-5pm, Sat 11-3 pm. Other dates/times by appointment.

programs.name: Museum visit
programs.description: A drop-in visit to the permanent displays, feature exhibits and revolving art gallery, with volunteers on hand. The page says admission is free, and further down that admission is by donation. Things named on the page include a Story Wall of clips about local events, the historical wooden 49th parallel town marker, a re-curve bow by local maker Art Williams, a miniature Victorian home and some children's toys. The museum, gift shop, gallery and Learning Centre are all in the one building.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the display rooms looking at objects from the town's mining, lumber and railway past, read the Story Wall, and find the miniature Victorian house and the old children's toys.
programs.our_note: It is one building with the gift shop by the door, so a small group can see it in well under an hour. Volunteers run the place, so ring ahead even within the posted opening hours to be sure someone is there for a group.
programs.practical_summary: Free to get in, indoors, with a wheelchair ramp and a bathroom downstairs in the Learning Centre. Nothing is published about lunch space, bus parking or how many children they can take at once.
programs.evidence: Admission is free. Leashed, well-mannered pets are welcome.

programs.name: Walking heritage tour
programs.description: The museum page says walking heritage tours are available by appointment, and gives two phone numbers to call. No price, length, route, group size or age range is published.
programs.our_note: This is the one thing here that gets children outside and moving, but all of it has to be arranged by phone. Ask how long the route is before you commit a group of little ones to it.
programs.practical_summary: Booked by appointment on the phone, and nothing about cost, length or group size is published.
programs.evidence: Walking heritage tours available by appointment.

programs.name: Historically Speaking talk for groups
programs.description: Historically Speaking is the Society's series of talks on local history, described as relevant to today's concerns while based on the roots of the past. Past presentations can be requested in person for groups of 10 or more, by donation, or watched free on the Society's YouTube channel. No age range, length or venue is given, and the site does not say whether they come to you or you come to them.
programs.our_note: This is a talk with slides, so it suits older children who can sit and listen rather than a preschool group. Ask which topics they can actually deliver, because what is listed is past presentations.
programs.practical_summary: For groups of 10 or more, by donation, with no set price. Nothing is published about how long it runs or where it happens.
programs.evidence: past presentations are available in person by request to groups of 10 or more (by donation)or free via YouTube.

gaps: This is a separate site from the Ladysmith Archives and the Ladysmith Industrial Heritage Museum, which are two other rows in the tracker. All three are run by the Ladysmith and District Historical Society on the same website, but the museum is at 721 1st Avenue, the archives at 1115 1st Avenue and the industrial heritage site at the former Comox Logging and Rail yard. This record is not a duplicate of either.
youngest age welcomed is not stated, and nothing on the site says whether daycare or preschool groups are taken.
capacity is not stated for the museum itself. Only the Historically Speaking talks give a number, and that is a minimum of 10 rather than a maximum.
lead time for a group visit is not stated. The only booking language is by appointment.
indoor lunch space is not stated. The Learning Centre has a small kitchenette but the page describes it as a rentable room rather than somewhere a group can eat.
bus parking and any parking at all are not mentioned.

The Learning Centre is described as suitable for educational interactive programs and activities for students and adult groups, and as currently developing community programming including movie matinees, speakers and arts and crafts. No specific children's programme is published, so none was recorded. Room rental prices are quoted by email.
price for a walking heritage tour is not published.

values: Open Friday noon to 2pm., Sat 11-3pm, and by appointment during winter
conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different opening hours. One says weekdays 10 to 5 and Saturday 11 to 3, the other says Friday noon to 2 and Saturday 11 to 3. We use the first. Worth checking when you book.
The museum page says admission is free in one place and by donation in another. Either way nobody will turn a group away, but take some cash if you want to leave something.
